subject: paper:faraone-2021-consensus
quote: ADHD can only be diagnosed by a licensed clinician who interviews the parent or caregiver and/or patient to document criteria for the disorder. It cannot be diagnosed by rating scales alone, neuropsychological tests, or methods for imaging the brain.
rationale: Verbatim from the PMC full text (PMC8328933), numbered Conclusion 14. The strongest single statement that no instrument — screener, cognitive test or scan — is itself diagnostic.

subject: paper:faraone-2021-consensus
quote: ADHD can only be diagnosed by a licensed clinician who interviews the parent or caregiver and/or patient to document criteria for the disorder. It cannot be diagnosed by rating scales alone, neuropsychological tests, or methods for imaging the brain.
rationale: Same Conclusion 14, applied indirectly: since only a clinician interview can diagnose and a rating scale cannot, a positive self-screen is precisely a reason to seek clinical evaluation rather than a conclusion. Medium — the paper states the diagnostic rule, the screen-warrants-evaluation inference is ours.

subject: paper:kooij-2019-consensus
quote: The clinical interview is essential for diagnosing ADHD in adults, which investigates the characteristic symptoms and impairments of ADHD in both childhood and adulthood.
rationale: Verified against the fetched full-text PDF (pdftotext). European consensus that the interview — not a questionnaire — carries the diagnosis, and must span both childhood and adult symptoms.

subject: paper:kooij-2019-consensus
quote: In such cases, the presence of a collateral informant (generally a parent or spouse) is of great value.
rationale: Verified against the fetched PDF. Follows the statement that adults with poor retrospective recall of childhood behaviours may miss the diagnosis; the collateral informant is the recommended remedy.

subject: paper:mannuzza-2002-recall
quote: Positive predictive value was 0.27, i.e., of all adults retrospectively given a diagnosis of childhood ADHD, only 27% would be correctly identified.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Quantifies how unreliable adult recall of childhood ADHD is in general-population settings — the core problem for a first adult diagnosis without childhood records.

subject: paper:mannuzza-2002-recall
quote: The results stress the importance of obtaining contemporaneous information on childhood symptoms in establishing a childhood history of ADHD.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The authors' own remedy: use records made at the time, not adult memory — the same conclusion Kooij reaches via collateral informants.

subject: paper:sibley-2012-informants
quote: Parent report was more diagnostically sensitive than self-report. Young adults with ADHD tended to underreport current symptoms, while young adults without ADHD tended to overreport symptoms.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Empirical case that self-report alone misleads in young adults — ADHD adults underreport — so informant reports carry real diagnostic weight.
